latestRelease.title: v1.40.1
latestRelease.notes:
## This is a patch release.

### What's Changed

- Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following `AUTH`, `SELECT`, `HELLO`, `CLIENT`, or `RESET` now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state ([#8016](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8016)).
- Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation ([#8011](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8011), [#8014](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8014)).

Full Changelog: [v1.40.0...v1.40.1](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.40.0...v1.40.1)
highlights: Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following AUTH, SELECT, HELLO, CLIENT, or RESET now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state (#8016).
Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation (#8011, #8014).

signals.title: Return RESP3 null for empty XREAD and XREADGROUP replies
signals.text: Under RESP3, XREAD and XREADGROUP return *-1 when no entries are available or a BLOCK timeout occurs. Redis returns the RESP3 null value (_\r\n) instead. Update these paths to emit RESP3 null replies while preserving *-1 for RESP2.

signals.text: Automated regression triage opened this issue. - Test: `dragonfly/connection_test.py::test_client_pause_v2_inflight_async_write_gap[df_factory0]` - Backend: iouring - Commit: 5f8de13f7d330c2a997a4bd2080be5008986e839 - Run: https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31767696825 - Marker: run/31767696825/attempt/1 ``` Reason: redis.exceptions.ResponseError: Failed to pause all running clients __________ test_client_pause_v2_inflight_async_write_gap[df_factory0] __________ df_server = :46593 @pytest.mark.opt_only # run against release/optimized build only @pytest.mark.exclude_epoll @dfly_args( { "proactor_threads": 4, "enable_resp_io_loop_v2": "true", # Tiered storage keeps a command in-flight on a thread-idle disk read, so CLIENT # PAUSE's fiber rendezvous can't implicitly wait for it and mask the bug. "tiered_prefix": "/tmp/tiered/pause_v2_backing", "tiered_offload_threshold": "1.0", "tiered_experimental_cooling": "false", "maxmemory": "2G", } ) async def test_client_pause_v2_inflight_async_write_gap(df_server: DflyInstance): """Regression: an in-flight async command on the V2 loop must keep CLIENT PAUSE waiting. A tiered APPEND parks the shard fiber on a disk read, so the command stays in-flight while returning a tiny reply. CLIENT PAUSE WRITE must not return until it completes. Tuning parameter: VALUE_BYTES (make the disk read long enough to stay in-flight). """ # Skip for V1 even if workflow injected --df enable_resp_io_loop_v2=false, which overrides the @dfly_args default above. if not is_resp_io_loop_v2(df_server): pytest.skip("targets the V2 io loop deferred-checkpoint path") VALUE_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024 # 256MB populator = df_server.client() writer = df_server.client() pauser = df_server.client() await populator.execute_command("DEBUG", "POPULATE", 1, "huge", VALUE_BYTES, "RAND") keys = await populator.keys("huge*") assert len(keys) == 1 big_key = keys[0] # Wait until the value is offloaded to disk (else APPEND reads from memory instantly). async with async_timeout.timeout(60): while int((await populator.info("TIERED")).get("tiered_entries", 0)) < 1: await asyncio.sleep(0.2) # Async write that must fetch the whole value from disk. Race them: a correct server writes # the APPEND reply before releasing the pause checkpoint, so APPEND wins. If PAUSE wins, the # write slipped past CLIENT PAUSE - the bug. (A sleep+snapshot check masks it or is racy.) pause_task = asyncio.create_task(pauser.execute_command("CLIENT", "PAUSE", "5000", "WRITE")) done, _ = await asyncio.wait({pause_task, inflight}, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED) pause_beat_inflight = pause_task in done and inflight not in done # Let both finish so the pauser/writer connections are idle before teardown. > assert await asyncio.wait_for(pause_task, timeout=60) == "OK" ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ VALUE_BYTES = 268435456 _ = {<Task pending name='Task-32212' coro=<Redis.execute_command() running at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/redis/asyncio/client.py:782> wait_for=<Future pending cb=[Task.task_wakeup()]>>} big_key = 'huge:0' df_server = :46593 done = {<Task finished name='Task-32213' coro=<Redis.execute_command() done, defined at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/redis/asyncio/client.py:760> exception=server:ResponseError>} inflight = <Task pending name='Task-32212' coro=<Redis.execute_command() running at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/redis/asyncio/client.py:782> wait_for=<Future pending cb=[Task.task_wakeup()]>> keys = ['huge:0'] pause_beat_inflight = True pause_task = <Task finished name='Task-32213' coro=<Redis.execute_command() done, defined at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/redis/asyncio/client.py:760> exception=server:ResponseError> pauser = <redis.asyncio.client.Redis(<redis.asyncio.connection.ConnectionPool(<redis.asyncio.connection.Connection(db=0,usernam...tocol=2,host=localhost,port=46593,socket_connect_timeout=None,socket_keepalive=None,socket_keepalive_options=None)>)>)> populator = <redis.asyncio.client.Redis(<redis.asyncio.connection.ConnectionPool( ```

signals.title: ZMPOP RESP2 reply is incompatibile with Redis
signals.text:
# `ZMPOP` returns the wrong RESP2 null type when no member can be popped **NOTE**: I found this issue when adding `dragonfly` to PhpRedis' CI (https://github.com/phpredis/phpredis/pull/2907). This surfaced about half a dozen reply shape incompatibilities with Redis. If perfect compatibility isn't a goal of dragonfly just let me know and I can instead update our tests **Describe the bug** When no member can be popped, Dragonfly returns a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1
`) instead of the null array (`*-1
`) returned by Redis. RESP2 null bulk strings and null arrays are distinct wire types even though some clients map both to the same language-level value. PhpRedis parses `ZMPOP` with its multi-bulk response parser. Dragonfly's null bulk string does not match the expected aggregate response type, so PhpRedis rejects the response and returns `false` instead of the expected empty result or `null`. **To Reproduce** 1. Connect using RESP2 to databases where `zs` does not exist or is empty. 2. Run `ZMPOP 1 zs MIN` against Redis and Dragonfly. 3. Compare the wire responses. In the example below, port 6379 is Redis and port 9999 is Dragonfly. ```console $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 6379 *-1 $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 $-1 ``` **Expected behavior** Like Redis, Dragonfly should return a RESP2 null array: ```text *-1
 ``` `ZMPOP` otherwise returns an aggregate containing the selected key and popped members, so its nil result should retain the aggregate response type. **Screenshots** Not applicable; the raw protocol responses are included above. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Not recorded - Kernel: Not recorded - Containerized?: Not recorded - Dragonfly Version: `df-v1.39.0` Redis control version: `8.9.241` Protocol: RESP2 **Reproducible Code Snippet** ```sh printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 ``` **Additional context** With `Redis::OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL` enabled, PhpRedis recognizes a null array as an empty `ZMPOP` result and returns it to PHP as `null`. This mismatch causes `Redis_Test::testZmpop` to fail: ```text Assertion failed: testZmpop - (false) !== (null) ``` Dragonfly's `ZMPopGeneric` empty-result path calls `SendNull()`: - [ZMPOP implementation](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/server/zset_family.cc) - [RESP reply builder](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/facade/reply_builder.cc) For RESP2, `SendNull()` emits `$-1
`. The reply builder has a distinct `SendNullArray()` method which emits `*-1
`. Dragonfly also returns `$-1
` for an empty or timed-out `BZMPOP`. The current PhpRedis `testBZmpop` only asserts the default `false` result, so it does not expose the type mismatch through `OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL`.
signals.author: michael-grunder

signals.title: ZADD GT/LT are silently ignored once a sorted set leaves listpack encoding
signals.text:
## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` are silently ignored for sorted sets that are not listpack-encoded. The flag is dropped with no error and the command behaves like a plain `ZADD`, so the score is overwritten unconditionally. Two independent conditions push a zset out of listpack encoding, and either one is enough to trigger this: - any member longer than **32 bytes** - more than **128 members** `NX` continues to behave correctly on the same keys, so this looks specific to GT/LT handling rather than to option parsing in general. Reproduced on **v1.39.0** and **v1.40.1** (latest at time of writing). Redis 7.4.10 is correct in every case, including at `skiplist` encoding. ## Reproduction ``` $ redis-cli DEL k $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 10 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # 33-byte member, inserts $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 3 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # must be a no-op: 3 < 10 $ redis-cli ZSCORE k aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "3" # expected "10" ``` The same member at 32 bytes returns `"10"` as expected. A self-contained script covering both boundaries and the `NX` contrast case: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u IMAGE="${1:-docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v1.40.1}" NAME="zadd_gtlt_repro_$$" docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 if [[ "$IMAGE" == *dragonfly* ]]; then docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" --logtostderr >/dev/null else docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" >/dev/null fi sleep 4 C() { docker exec "$NAME" redis-cli "$@"; } echo "server: $(C INFO server | grep -E 'dragonfly_version|redis_version' | tr -d '')" fail=0 check() { local label="$1" flag="$2" first="$3" second="$4" expect="$5" member="$6" local key="k$RANDOM$RANDOM" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$first" "$member" >/dev/null # insert C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$second" "$member" >/dev/null # must NOT apply local got; got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$member" | tr -d '') local status=OK if [[ "$got" != "$expect" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD %s %-5s -> %-5s (want %-5s) %s
' \ "$label" "$flag" "$second" "$got" "$expect" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null } echo "--- member length ---" check "1-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "x" check "32-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..32})" check "33-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" check "33-byte member" LT 3 10 3 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" echo "--- member count (all members 2 bytes) ---" for count in 128 129; do key="c$count" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null { for i in $(seq 1 "$count"); do echo "ZADD $key GT 10 m$i"; done; } \ | docker exec -i "$NAME" redis-cli >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" GT 3 m1 >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" m1 | tr -d '') status=OK if [[ "$got" != "10" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD GT 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "$count members" "$got" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null done echo "--- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast ---" key="nx$RANDOM"; M="$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" 10 "$M" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" NX 3 "$M" >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$M" | tr -d '') printf ' %-34s ZADD NX 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "33-byte member" "$got" \ "$([[ "$got" == 10 ]] && echo OK || echo BROKEN)" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 echo [[ $fail -eq 0 ]] && echo "RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held" || echo "RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings" exit $fail ``` ## Observed output Dragonfly v1.40.1 (identical on v1.39.0): ``` server: redis_version:7.4.0 dragonfly_version:df-v1.40.1 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 10 (want 3 ) BROKEN --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings ``` Redis 7.4.10, same script: ``` server: redis_version:7.4.10 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 3 (want 3 ) OK --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held ``` ## Expected behaviour Per the `ZADD` contract, `GT` updates an existing member only if the new score is greater than the current one, and `LT` only if it is less. Neither prevents inserting an absent member. This should hold regardless of the internal encoding. ## Environment - Dragonfly `v1.39.0` and `v1.40.1`, official images, default flags plus `--logtostderr` - Docker on macOS (arm64) - Reference: `redis:7.4-alpine` (7.4.10), default config ## Why this matters `ZADD GT`/`LT` is the only native atomic max/min in the Redis API, so it is the natural primitive for tracking running extrema without a read-modify-write or a Lua script. Because the flag is dropped silently rather than rejected, the failure surfaces as plausible-looking but wrong data — a stored extremum becomes "the most recently written value" — and only for keys that happen to have grown past a threshold. There is no error and no metric to alert on. Small smoke tests will pass, which makes this easy to adopt and hard to detect: we validated the primitive with short members on an empty key, built on it, and only caught the problem when a concurrency test on realistic key shapes reported a minimum of 919.5 where the true minimum was 81. Rejecting GT/LT with an error on unsupported encodings would at least be safe, but matching Redis semantics is obviously preferable.
signals.author: dbwcanalhas

signals.title: ci(tests): add scheduled e2e workflow for ioredis client
signals.text: ## What Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, `.github/workflows/ioredis-tests.yml`, that runs the existing [ioredis](https://github.com/luin/ioredis) end-to-end test suite against a freshly built Dragonfly binary every day, and points to it from `tests/README.md`. ## Why (closes part of #383) `#383` asked for e2e coverage of the `ioredis` client. Looking at the history: - `tests/integration/ioredis.Dockerfile` and `tests/integration/run_ioredis_on_docker.sh` (added in #394 / #459) already give a local script + README instructions for running the curated ioredis test suite against Dragonfly (deliverables 1 & 2 from the issue). - What was still missing is what @romange asked for in the issue thread: *"we just need to run them via the testing pipeline on github"*. There was no CI workflow exercising these tests — `ioredis`/`node-redis`/`jedis` Dockerfiles are all local-only, and grepping every workflow in `.github/workflows` shows none of them touch `tests/integration`. - The repo already has exactly this pattern for another ioredis-based client, `bullmq-tests.yml` (nightly scheduled job, builds Dragonfly from source, installs Node, runs the client's own test suite with a skip-list). This PR mirrors that same structure for `ioredis` itself, reusing the pre-existing `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` skip/grep list rather than duplicating it. ## What this does NOT do - It does not touch the existing local Docker scripts — those keep working as-is for local development. - It does not attempt the issue's "bonus" deliverable (a bespoke Dragonfly-authored pub/sub regression test); that's a separate, larger piece of work and is left as a possible follow-up so this PR stays focused on the CI-wiring gap. ## Testing Since building the full C++ project wasn't practical in my environment, I validated the actual test-execution path the workflow runs: - Started the official `dragonfly` Docker image (`--cluster_mode=emulated --lock_on_hashtags --dbfilename=`, same flags as `bullmq-tests.yml` uses for Dragonfly). - Cloned `luin/ioredis`, ran `npm install`, then ran the exact command the new workflow runs: `npm run env -- TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true NODE_ENV=test ./run_tests.sh` using the repo's own `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` as `run_tests.sh`. - Result: **493 passing / 2 failing**, both failures being `Timeout of 8000ms exceeded` on tests unrelated to correctness (a large-pipeline timing test and a cluster startup-nodes teardown hook) — consistent with the constrained local sandbox rather than a real regression. I couldn't run the pre-commit C++/format hooks in this environment (no C++ toolchain available), but this PR only touches a workflow YAML file and a doc file, so `clang-format`/`black` are not applicable. Closes (partially) #383

signals.title: fix(facade): Handle RESP3 null array response
signals.text: RESP3 expects "_\r\n" for a null array, but SendNullArray() always sent RESP2's "*-1\r\n" regardless of protocol. This fixed null replies under RESP3 for XREAD, XREADGROUP, BLPOP, BRPOP, BZPOPMIN, and BZPOPMAX. Closes #8076 <!-- **Commits Must Be Signed and Your PR title must conform to the conventional commit spec** * See: https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md * Please follow the section on `pre-commit hooks`, a linter will validate before you push Example PR Title: <type>(<scope>)!: <description> * `type` = bug, chore, feat, fix, docs, build, style, refactor, perf, test * `!` = OPTIONAL: signals a breaking change * `scope` = Optional when `type` is "chore" or "docs" * `description` = short description of the change Examples: * chore(examples): Clarify `docker` usage #120 * docs(readme): Fix Example Links #121 * feat(ingest)!: Add new ingest #122 * fix(ingest): Refactor for loop to list comprehension #123 -->

signals.title: fix(zset): honor GT/LT flags for skiplist-encoded sorted sets
signals.text: ## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` were silently ignored once a sorted set left listpack encoding (i.e. once it had a member longer than 32 bytes, or more than 128 members). The score was overwritten unconditionally, as if the command were a plain `ZADD`, with no error. Root cause: the GT/LT clamp check exists in the listpack path (`ZsetAdd` in `zset_family.cc`) but was missing entirely from the skiplist path (`SortedMap::AddElem` in `sorted_map.cc`), which just updated the score whenever the element already existed. ## Fix Add the same GT/LT clamp to `SortedMap::AddElem`: if `LT` and the new score isn't lower, or `GT` and the new score isn't higher, treat the update as a no-op (matching the listpack path and Redis semantics). ## Test plan - Added `ZSetFamilyTest.AddGtLtSkiplist`, using a 33-byte member to force skiplist encoding immediately, covering both GT and LT in both the no-op and update directions. - `ninja zset_family_test && ./zset_family_test --gtest_filter='*GtLt*:*Add*'` — all 5 tests pass. - `pre-commit` clang-format check passes on both changed files. Fixes #8089
signals.author: Shikha-code36

signals.title: fix: reply with a null array for empty ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP
signals.text: When no element can be popped, ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP replied with a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1\r\n`) instead of the null array (`*-1\r\n`) expected for aggregate-reply commands, so strict clients (e.g. PhpRedis) rejected the reply. Builds on #8085, which made `SendNullArray()` protocol-aware (RESP2 `*-1`, RESP3 `_`). Changes: - The empty/timeout reply paths of ZMPOP/BZMPOP (`zset_family.cc`) and LMPOP/BLMPOP (`list_family.cc`) use `SendNullArray()`. - BLMPOP now maps non-OK statuses the same way BLPOP does; a `WRONGTYPE` error is no longer swallowed into a null reply. - `InterpreterReplier::SendNullArray()` converts a null-array reply to Lua `false` (previously it produced an empty table and called `PostItem()` twice, which hit a DCHECK in debug builds when reached, e.g. via `EVAL` calling `XINFO STREAM` on an empty stream). - Simplify `SendNullArray()` to a ternary, matching `SendNull()`. - Tests: existing empty/timeout assertions now expect the null array; added a BLMPOP wrong-type test, a Lua conversion test, and a raw-socket pytest asserting the exact wire bytes under RESP2 and RESP3 (draining the full HELLO reply via `_read_resp_frame`). Fixes #8087
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: fix(tests): extend pause wait (Fixes #8079)
signals.text: CI failed because the intentional 256 MB tiered read exceeded the one-second CLIENT PAUSE setup timeout, including its retry (total 2 seconds). Extend the regression's pause wait to 30 seconds so the modified test continues to verify that CLIENT PAUSE returns only after the in-flight asynchronous write has completed.

signals.title: feat(server): make conn_use_incoming_cpu runtime mutable
signals.text: ## Summary `conn_use_incoming_cpu` controls how new connections are distributed across proactor threads, and `Listener::PickConnectionProactor` already reads it on every accept — but it is not registered in the config registry, so changing it requires a restart. This PR registers it as mutable, so `CONFIG SET conn_use_incoming_cpu <bool>` takes effect immediately for new connections. No behavior change unless CONFIG SET is used. ## Motivation The flag's own comment notes it is only safe with correct RPS tuning: *"connections will be handled only on the CPUs that handle the softirqs for the incoming packets. To avoid imbalance in CPU load, RPS tuning is strongly advised."* In practice, steering misconfiguration is discovered in production. On one of our deployments (144 vCPUs; NIC IRQs pinned to CPUs 0–15, Dragonfly on 16–143) an RPS mask covering only part of the worker range concentrated **all** connections on 47 of 128 threads. A latency blip then became a self-feeding reconnect storm: the overloaded connection threads slowed replies, clients timed out and reconnected, and every new connection landed on the same hot threads. The only remedies were adding a replica or restarting the loaded master. With the flag mutable, an operator can flip placement to round-robin at runtime to break such a loop (optionally recycling clients gradually with `CLIENT KILL`), and flip it back once steering is fixed — no restart needed. ## Changes - Register `conn_use_incoming_cpu` as mutable in the config registry. - Add a pytest covering the `CONFIG GET`/`SET` round-trip and that new connections are served after toggling. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: test(fuzz): repair seed corpus so every seed executes and harden coverage guard
signals.text: Audited every command the RESP and memcache fuzzers emit and fixed the seed corpus so each seed replays cleanly on a fresh fuzz server. A seed that dead-ends in an error reply (unknown command, arity, syntax, wrong-type, or missing prior state) gives the command-level mutator nothing valid to mutate; 91 seeds across 78 files were doing exactly that. Changes: - **3 seeds never executed at all**: `save_cf`, `save_cms`, `save_topk` were bare-LF framed instead of CRLF (server rejects the first byte), and `append_prepend.mc` had a broken data-block byte count. All reframed. - **Phantom commands removed**: `GEOSEARCHSTORE` and `OBJECT` are not registered in Dragonfly; replaced with real store/introspection forms. - **~30 arity/syntax/state failures fixed** (e.g. `HEXPIRE` missing `FIELDS`, `LMOVE` missing direction, `ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZDIFFSTORE` bad numkeys, `EVALSHA` with an unloaded sha, `FUNCTION` subcommands other than `FLUSH`, `XSETID` below top ID, out-of-range `EXPIREAT`). - **Removed commands that can never succeed under the fuzz config** (cluster-only, ACL-file, AUTH, restricted flush, non-cluster sharded pub/sub) and swapped in executing equivalents. - **New seeds**: `resp3_ops.resp` (first seed to switch to RESP3 via `HELLO 3` - that whole reply-serialization path was unfuzzed) and three `*_gap.resp` option-grammar depth seeds. - **Coverage guard hardened**: `check_fuzz_coverage.py` now strict-parses each seed with the mutator's own parser (a mis-framed seed is a hard failure) for both RESP and memcache, counts commands in command position only, and its `KNOWN_GAPS` list is now empty. Mutators drop dispatch-dead commands and gain correct option/flag vocabularies; dictionaries updated.

signal.title: fix: reply with a null array for empty ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP
signal.text: When no element can be popped, ZMPOP/BZMPOP/LMPOP/BLMPOP replied with a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1\r\n`) instead of the null array (`*-1\r\n`) expected for aggregate-reply commands, so strict clients (e.g. PhpRedis) rejected the reply. Builds on #8085, which made `SendNullArray()` protocol-aware (RESP2 `*-1`, RESP3 `_`). Changes: - The empty/timeout reply paths of ZMPOP/BZMPOP (`zset_family.cc`) and LMPOP/BLMPOP (`list_family.cc`) use `SendNullArray()`. - BLMPOP now maps non-OK statuses the same way BLPOP does; a `WRONGTYPE` error is no longer swallowed into a null reply. - `InterpreterReplier::SendNullArray()` converts a null-array reply to Lua `false` (previously it produced an empty table and called `PostItem()` twice, which hit a DCHECK in debug builds when reached, e.g. via `EVAL` calling `XINFO STREAM` on an empty stream). - Simplify `SendNullArray()` to a ternary, matching `SendNull()`. - Tests: existing empty/timeout assertions now expect the null array; added a BLMPOP wrong-type test, a Lua conversion test, and a raw-socket pytest asserting the exact wire bytes under RESP2 and RESP3 (draining the full HELLO reply via `_read_resp_frame`). Fixes #8087

signal.title: ZMPOP RESP2 reply is incompatibile with Redis
signal.text:
# `ZMPOP` returns the wrong RESP2 null type when no member can be popped **NOTE**: I found this issue when adding `dragonfly` to PhpRedis' CI (https://github.com/phpredis/phpredis/pull/2907). This surfaced about half a dozen reply shape incompatibilities with Redis. If perfect compatibility isn't a goal of dragonfly just let me know and I can instead update our tests **Describe the bug** When no member can be popped, Dragonfly returns a RESP2 null bulk string (`$-1
`) instead of the null array (`*-1
`) returned by Redis. RESP2 null bulk strings and null arrays are distinct wire types even though some clients map both to the same language-level value. PhpRedis parses `ZMPOP` with its multi-bulk response parser. Dragonfly's null bulk string does not match the expected aggregate response type, so PhpRedis rejects the response and returns `false` instead of the expected empty result or `null`. **To Reproduce** 1. Connect using RESP2 to databases where `zs` does not exist or is empty. 2. Run `ZMPOP 1 zs MIN` against Redis and Dragonfly. 3. Compare the wire responses. In the example below, port 6379 is Redis and port 9999 is Dragonfly. ```console $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 6379 *-1 $ printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 $-1 ``` **Expected behavior** Like Redis, Dragonfly should return a RESP2 null array: ```text *-1
 ``` `ZMPOP` otherwise returns an aggregate containing the selected key and popped members, so its nil result should retain the aggregate response type. **Screenshots** Not applicable; the raw protocol responses are included above. **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Not recorded - Kernel: Not recorded - Containerized?: Not recorded - Dragonfly Version: `df-v1.39.0` Redis control version: `8.9.241` Protocol: RESP2 **Reproducible Code Snippet** ```sh printf 'ZMPOP 1 zs MIN
' | nc -N localhost 9999 ``` **Additional context** With `Redis::OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL` enabled, PhpRedis recognizes a null array as an empty `ZMPOP` result and returns it to PHP as `null`. This mismatch causes `Redis_Test::testZmpop` to fail: ```text Assertion failed: testZmpop - (false) !== (null) ``` Dragonfly's `ZMPopGeneric` empty-result path calls `SendNull()`: - [ZMPOP implementation](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/server/zset_family.cc) - [RESP reply builder](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/src/facade/reply_builder.cc) For RESP2, `SendNull()` emits `$-1
`. The reply builder has a distinct `SendNullArray()` method which emits `*-1
`. Dragonfly also returns `$-1
` for an empty or timed-out `BZMPOP`. The current PhpRedis `testBZmpop` only asserts the default `false` result, so it does not expose the type mismatch through `OPT_NULL_MULTIBULK_AS_NULL`.
signal.author: michael-grunder

signal.title: ZADD GT/LT are silently ignored once a sorted set leaves listpack encoding
signal.text:
## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` are silently ignored for sorted sets that are not listpack-encoded. The flag is dropped with no error and the command behaves like a plain `ZADD`, so the score is overwritten unconditionally. Two independent conditions push a zset out of listpack encoding, and either one is enough to trigger this: - any member longer than **32 bytes** - more than **128 members** `NX` continues to behave correctly on the same keys, so this looks specific to GT/LT handling rather than to option parsing in general. Reproduced on **v1.39.0** and **v1.40.1** (latest at time of writing). Redis 7.4.10 is correct in every case, including at `skiplist` encoding. ## Reproduction ``` $ redis-cli DEL k $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 10 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # 33-byte member, inserts $ redis-cli ZADD k GT 3 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa # must be a no-op: 3 < 10 $ redis-cli ZSCORE k aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa "3" # expected "10" ``` The same member at 32 bytes returns `"10"` as expected. A self-contained script covering both boundaries and the `NX` contrast case: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -u IMAGE="${1:-docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v1.40.1}" NAME="zadd_gtlt_repro_$$" docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 if [[ "$IMAGE" == *dragonfly* ]]; then docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" --logtostderr >/dev/null else docker run -d --name "$NAME" "$IMAGE" >/dev/null fi sleep 4 C() { docker exec "$NAME" redis-cli "$@"; } echo "server: $(C INFO server | grep -E 'dragonfly_version|redis_version' | tr -d '')" fail=0 check() { local label="$1" flag="$2" first="$3" second="$4" expect="$5" member="$6" local key="k$RANDOM$RANDOM" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$first" "$member" >/dev/null # insert C ZADD "$key" "$flag" "$second" "$member" >/dev/null # must NOT apply local got; got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$member" | tr -d '') local status=OK if [[ "$got" != "$expect" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD %s %-5s -> %-5s (want %-5s) %s
' \ "$label" "$flag" "$second" "$got" "$expect" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null } echo "--- member length ---" check "1-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "x" check "32-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..32})" check "33-byte member" GT 10 3 10 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" check "33-byte member" LT 3 10 3 "$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" echo "--- member count (all members 2 bytes) ---" for count in 128 129; do key="c$count" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null { for i in $(seq 1 "$count"); do echo "ZADD $key GT 10 m$i"; done; } \ | docker exec -i "$NAME" redis-cli >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" GT 3 m1 >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" m1 | tr -d '') status=OK if [[ "$got" != "10" ]]; then status=BROKEN; fail=1; fi printf ' %-34s ZADD GT 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "$count members" "$got" "$status" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null done echo "--- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast ---" key="nx$RANDOM"; M="$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..33})" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" 10 "$M" >/dev/null C ZADD "$key" NX 3 "$M" >/dev/null got=$(C ZSCORE "$key" "$M" | tr -d '') printf ' %-34s ZADD NX 3 -> %-5s (want 10 ) %s
' "33-byte member" "$got" \ "$([[ "$got" == 10 ]] && echo OK || echo BROKEN)" C DEL "$key" >/dev/null docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 echo [[ $fail -eq 0 ]] && echo "RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held" || echo "RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings" exit $fail ``` ## Observed output Dragonfly v1.40.1 (identical on v1.39.0): ``` server: redis_version:7.4.0 dragonfly_version:df-v1.40.1 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 10 (want 3 ) BROKEN --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 3 (want 10 ) BROKEN --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: GT/LT ignored in some encodings ``` Redis 7.4.10, same script: ``` server: redis_version:7.4.10 --- member length --- 1-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 32-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 33-byte member ZADD LT 10 -> 3 (want 3 ) OK --- member count (all members 2 bytes) --- 128 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK 129 members ZADD GT 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK --- NX on a 33-byte member, for contrast --- 33-byte member ZADD NX 3 -> 10 (want 10 ) OK RESULT: all GT/LT clamps held ``` ## Expected behaviour Per the `ZADD` contract, `GT` updates an existing member only if the new score is greater than the current one, and `LT` only if it is less. Neither prevents inserting an absent member. This should hold regardless of the internal encoding. ## Environment - Dragonfly `v1.39.0` and `v1.40.1`, official images, default flags plus `--logtostderr` - Docker on macOS (arm64) - Reference: `redis:7.4-alpine` (7.4.10), default config ## Why this matters `ZADD GT`/`LT` is the only native atomic max/min in the Redis API, so it is the natural primitive for tracking running extrema without a read-modify-write or a Lua script. Because the flag is dropped silently rather than rejected, the failure surfaces as plausible-looking but wrong data — a stored extremum becomes "the most recently written value" — and only for keys that happen to have grown past a threshold. There is no error and no metric to alert on. Small smoke tests will pass, which makes this easy to adopt and hard to detect: we validated the primitive with short members on an empty key, built on it, and only caught the problem when a concurrency test on realistic key shapes reported a minimum of 919.5 where the true minimum was 81. Rejecting GT/LT with an error on unsupported encodings would at least be safe, but matching Redis semantics is obviously preferable.
signal.author: dbwcanalhas

signal.title: fix(zset): honor GT/LT flags for skiplist-encoded sorted sets
signal.text: ## Summary `ZADD ... GT` and `ZADD ... LT` were silently ignored once a sorted set left listpack encoding (i.e. once it had a member longer than 32 bytes, or more than 128 members). The score was overwritten unconditionally, as if the command were a plain `ZADD`, with no error. Root cause: the GT/LT clamp check exists in the listpack path (`ZsetAdd` in `zset_family.cc`) but was missing entirely from the skiplist path (`SortedMap::AddElem` in `sorted_map.cc`), which just updated the score whenever the element already existed. ## Fix Add the same GT/LT clamp to `SortedMap::AddElem`: if `LT` and the new score isn't lower, or `GT` and the new score isn't higher, treat the update as a no-op (matching the listpack path and Redis semantics). ## Test plan - Added `ZSetFamilyTest.AddGtLtSkiplist`, using a 33-byte member to force skiplist encoding immediately, covering both GT and LT in both the no-op and update directions. - `ninja zset_family_test && ./zset_family_test --gtest_filter='*GtLt*:*Add*'` — all 5 tests pass. - `pre-commit` clang-format check passes on both changed files. Fixes #8089
signal.author: Shikha-code36

signal.title: feat(server): make conn_use_incoming_cpu runtime mutable
signal.text: ## Summary `conn_use_incoming_cpu` controls how new connections are distributed across proactor threads, and `Listener::PickConnectionProactor` already reads it on every accept — but it is not registered in the config registry, so changing it requires a restart. This PR registers it as mutable, so `CONFIG SET conn_use_incoming_cpu <bool>` takes effect immediately for new connections. No behavior change unless CONFIG SET is used. ## Motivation The flag's own comment notes it is only safe with correct RPS tuning: *"connections will be handled only on the CPUs that handle the softirqs for the incoming packets. To avoid imbalance in CPU load, RPS tuning is strongly advised."* In practice, steering misconfiguration is discovered in production. On one of our deployments (144 vCPUs; NIC IRQs pinned to CPUs 0–15, Dragonfly on 16–143) an RPS mask covering only part of the worker range concentrated **all** connections on 47 of 128 threads. A latency blip then became a self-feeding reconnect storm: the overloaded connection threads slowed replies, clients timed out and reconnected, and every new connection landed on the same hot threads. The only remedies were adding a replica or restarting the loaded master. With the flag mutable, an operator can flip placement to round-robin at runtime to break such a loop (optionally recycling clients gradually with `CLIENT KILL`), and flip it back once steering is fixed — no restart needed. ## Changes - Register `conn_use_incoming_cpu` as mutable in the config registry. - Add a pytest covering the `CONFIG GET`/`SET` round-trip and that new connections are served after toggling. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: ci(tests): add scheduled e2e workflow for ioredis client
signal.text: ## What Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, `.github/workflows/ioredis-tests.yml`, that runs the existing [ioredis](https://github.com/luin/ioredis) end-to-end test suite against a freshly built Dragonfly binary every day, and points to it from `tests/README.md`. ## Why (closes part of #383) `#383` asked for e2e coverage of the `ioredis` client. Looking at the history: - `tests/integration/ioredis.Dockerfile` and `tests/integration/run_ioredis_on_docker.sh` (added in #394 / #459) already give a local script + README instructions for running the curated ioredis test suite against Dragonfly (deliverables 1 & 2 from the issue). - What was still missing is what @romange asked for in the issue thread: *"we just need to run them via the testing pipeline on github"*. There was no CI workflow exercising these tests — `ioredis`/`node-redis`/`jedis` Dockerfiles are all local-only, and grepping every workflow in `.github/workflows` shows none of them touch `tests/integration`. - The repo already has exactly this pattern for another ioredis-based client, `bullmq-tests.yml` (nightly scheduled job, builds Dragonfly from source, installs Node, runs the client's own test suite with a skip-list). This PR mirrors that same structure for `ioredis` itself, reusing the pre-existing `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` skip/grep list rather than duplicating it. ## What this does NOT do - It does not touch the existing local Docker scripts — those keep working as-is for local development. - It does not attempt the issue's "bonus" deliverable (a bespoke Dragonfly-authored pub/sub regression test); that's a separate, larger piece of work and is left as a possible follow-up so this PR stays focused on the CI-wiring gap. ## Testing Since building the full C++ project wasn't practical in my environment, I validated the actual test-execution path the workflow runs: - Started the official `dragonfly` Docker image (`--cluster_mode=emulated --lock_on_hashtags --dbfilename=`, same flags as `bullmq-tests.yml` uses for Dragonfly). - Cloned `luin/ioredis`, ran `npm install`, then ran the exact command the new workflow runs: `npm run env -- TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true NODE_ENV=test ./run_tests.sh` using the repo's own `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` as `run_tests.sh`. - Result: **493 passing / 2 failing**, both failures being `Timeout of 8000ms exceeded` on tests unrelated to correctness (a large-pipeline timing test and a cluster startup-nodes teardown hook) — consistent with the constrained local sandbox rather than a real regression. I couldn't run the pre-commit C++/format hooks in this environment (no C++ toolchain available), but this PR only touches a workflow YAML file and a doc file, so `clang-format`/`black` are not applicable. Closes (partially) #383

signal.title: fix(facade): Handle RESP3 null array response
signal.text: RESP3 expects "_\r\n" for a null array, but SendNullArray() always sent RESP2's "*-1\r\n" regardless of protocol. This fixed null replies under RESP3 for XREAD, XREADGROUP, BLPOP, BRPOP, BZPOPMIN, and BZPOPMAX. signal.title: Return RESP3 null for empty XREAD and XREADGROUP replies
signal.text: Under RESP3, XREAD and XREADGROUP return *-1 when no entries are available or a BLOCK timeout occurs. Redis returns the RESP3 null value (_\r\n) instead. Update these paths to emit RESP3 null replies while preserving *-1 for RESP2.

signal.title: fix(tests): extend pause wait (Fixes #8079)
signal.text: CI failed because the intentional 256 MB tiered read exceeded the one-second CLIENT PAUSE setup timeout, including its retry (total 2 seconds). Extend the regression's pause wait to 30 seconds so the modified test continues to verify that CLIENT PAUSE returns only after the in-flight asynchronous write has completed.
